message.content:
Based on the information from authoritative health sources, here is what you should know about treating a cold:

## Important Facts

**There is no cure for the common cold.** Colds are caused by viruses (most commonly rhinoviruses), and antibiotics do not work against viruses. Most colds improve on their own within 7 to 10 days.

## Over-the-Counter Medications for Symptom Relief

### Pain Relievers/Fever Reducers
- **Acetaminophen** (Tylenol) – for headaches, sore throat, fever, and minor aches
- **Ibuprofen** (Advil, Motrin) – an NSAID that helps with pain and inflammation
- **Aspirin** – for adults only; never give to children or teenagers due to risk of Reye's syndrome

### For Nasal Congestion
- **Decongestants** such as **pseudoephedrine** (note: oral phenylephrine has been found ineffective by the FDA as of 2024)
- **Nasal decongestant sprays** (like phenylephrine nasal spray) – but do not use for more than 3-5 days to avoid rebound congestion

### For Runny Nose and Sneezing
- **First-generation antihistamines** (like chlorpheniramine, doxylamine) may help reduce rhinorrhea and sneezing, though they have minimal effects on other symptoms and can cause drowsiness
- Second-generation antihistamines (like loratadine, fexofenadine) are generally not effective for cold symptoms

### For Cough
- **Dextromethorphan** – a cough suppressant
- **Guaifenesin** – an expectorant that thins mucus
- **Honey** – for adults and children over 1 year old (never give honey to infants under 1)

### Saline Nasal Products
- Saline nasal sprays, drops, or rinses can help keep nasal passages moist and loosen mucus

## Important Warnings

- **Children under 6 years old** should not use OTC cough/cold medicines without consulting a healthcare provider
- **Children under 4 years old** should not take OTC cold medicines containing antihistamines or decongestants
- Do not combine multiple medications with the same active ingredients to avoid accidental overdose
- If you have high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, or other chronic conditions, consult your doctor before using decongestants

## Non-Drug Measures That Help

- Get plenty of rest
- Drink plenty of fluids (water, juice, warm broth)
- Use a humidifier or cool-mist vaporizer
- Gargle with warm salt water for sore throat
- Sip warm liquids like tea or chicken soup
- Use throat lozenges (not for children under 4)

## When to Seek Medical Care

- Trouble breathing or fast breathing
- Dehydration
- Fever lasting more than 4 days
- Symptoms lasting more than 10 days without improvement
- Symptoms that improve then worsen
- Severe or concerning symptoms

**Note:** If you suspect COVID-19 or flu rather than a common cold, get tested as antiviral treatments are available and work best when started early.

---

Sources:
1. https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/treatment/index.html
2. https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/common-cold/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20351611
3. https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/common-cold/in-depth/cold-remedies/art-20046403
4. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/decongestants-antihistamines-cold
5. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/otc-cold-medicines
6. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1113448/
